editorial.marketOverview: The Nasdaq/QQQ three-session baseline remains bearish after the broad November 19 US selloff, with semiconductor underperformance, elevated VIX and weak breadth. Friday US cash-market reaction has not occurred at this review.
editorial.whatChanged: Reuters' November 20 Asian-session reporting adds a 3.2% regional daily fall and 8.3% weekly drawdown, reinforcing global AI risk aversion. These are additional observations of an existing deterioration rather than a fresh directional regime shift. Open Watch remains 171 curated events at its last verified repository timestamp.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Risk aversion is spreading across Asian technology equities while a strong dollar and expectations of tighter Fed policy constrain risk appetite. Treasury safe-haven buying is reported, but a synchronized 10Y/2Y curve cannot be computed. Futures indications are not evidence of Friday's actual QQQ or SOX cash performance.
editorial.threeDayPath: Friday November 20 is vulnerable to a failed rebound and elevated volatility; a stronger close with recovering semiconductor leadership could interrupt downside momentum. Monday November 23 should test whether Friday's breadth and chip leadership stabilize. Tuesday November 24 provides further follow-through confirmation around company earnings and macro developments.
editorial.bullCase: An oversold bounce is plausible following the multi-session decline. Sustained QQQ strength versus SPY, renewed SOX/SMH leadership, broader advancing participation and easing VXN/VIX would weaken the bearish thesis; the positive Anthropic IPO close is an isolated counterpoint.
editorial.bearCase: Thursday's Nasdaq decline, breadth deterioration and elevated volatility combine with Asia's sharp technology selloff and weaker overnight US futures to favor continuation risk. A Friday rebound that fails on poor breadth would confirm pressure into Monday.
